size_bands: Voluntary, unless national law requires it

IT.instrument: Legislative Decree No. 96 of 7 May 2026 (Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 125, 1 June 2026), in force 7 June 2026
IT.reporting: Thresholds, frequencies and first deadlines as in Article 9(2)-(4) of the Directive (art. 9(8)-(9)). The gaps, quartile bands and the 5% test are computed on livello retributivo, fixed and continuing pay, not on total pay (art. 3(1)(b), art. 10(1)(a))
IT.notes: Applying a national collective agreement signed by the unions comparatively most representative at national level is presumed to comply, classification included, unless individual discriminatory pay treatment is shown; its levels are the reference for work of equal value and an employer's own gender-neutral system may complement them (art. 4). Monitoring body at the Ministry of Labour (art. 14). Implementing decrees on data collection were due within 90 days of 7 June 2026 [to verify whether adopted]

PL.instrument: Labour Code amendment on transparency in recruitment, in force since December 2025; draft act on pay reporting and the right to information published 29 April 2026
PL.reporting: Draft: 250+ every year, 100-249 every three years; first reports 7 June 2027 (150+) and 7 June 2031 (100-149); later reports due by 31 March
PL.notes: Sources give 23 or 24 December 2025 for the recruitment rules. The draft enters into force six months after publication, so Poland missed 7 June 2026. Lockton's tracker (status at 23 September 2026) dates the revised draft 4 May 2026; not adopted by then

DE.instrument: No act adopted; Bundestag press notice on transposition, 16 July 2026
DE.reporting: Directive deadlines apply to the timetable once transposed; national rules not yet known
DE.notes: Germany missed 7 June 2026. The existing Entgelttransparenzgesetz (2017) stays in force until replaced [to verify on the final act]

ES.instrument: Draft Royal Decree published 3 August 2026, consultation until 24 August 2026
ES.reporting: Not final; the draft text sets the national timetable
ES.notes: Spain missed 7 June 2026. Existing pay register and pay audit duties (Royal Decree 902/2020) continue [to verify how the draft aligns them]. Lockton's tracker calls it a draft law published 3 August 2026, not yet adopted at 23 September 2026
